newsitem.title: USA: Georgia's Shevardnadze, in U.S., seeks investment.
newsitem.headline: Georgia's Shevardnadze, in U.S., seeks investment.

text.p: Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze appealed for investment in his troubled country on Thursday, highlighting a remarkable shift to stability and democracy after years of civil strife.
Shevardnadze told U.S. business leaders that Georgia was open to foreign investment in sectors ranging from energy to agriculture and from mining to machine building.
The Transcaucasian country was on a key transit route from Asia to Europe and would be a channel for Caspian Sea oil to European markets, he said.

"Only two or three years ago, Georgia was in a state of chaos and devastation. Civil war was raging and there was a lot of bloodshed," the Georgian leader told a meeting at the U.S. export guarantee agency OPIC.

"I do not quite want to call it a miracle, but it is probably in the range of a miracle. Within two or three years complete stablity has taken place, the rampage of gangs has ceased and the framework has been created for cooperation," he said.

Shevardnadze, a darling of Western governments when he was foreign minister of the former Soviet Union, has been seeking Western help to deal with separatists in the north and the west of Georgia, especially in the Black Sea area of Abkhazia.
Georgia lost control of Abkhazia, a lush subtropical region, when its disorganised military was driven out in 1993 after a year of fighting that killed more than 10,000 people.
Shevardnadze is due to visit the White House, the Pentagon and the United Nations during his U.S. visit, and will hold talks with World Bank and International Monetary Fund officials.
He said Georgia had received over $310 million from the two financial organisations and stressed that its economic reform programme was on track.
Inflation was set to fall to 11 percent this year, from 13.5 percent in 1996, and the economy was also growing strongly -- nine percent in the first half of the year, he said.
"Hyperinflation has been stopped and financial stability has been attained...the privatisation process is successfully under way," he said.
"My task as president of Georgia is to create conditions encouraging foreign investment in Georgia...and I assure you of every support in the successful implementation of your projects," he said.
